title: The 3 Best Pull-Up Bars Under $30
metaDescription: Our 3 picks for pull-up bars under $30, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at pull-up bars under $30 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Iron Gym Total Upper Body Workout Bar - Extreme Edition
products.blurb: Key specs: 5 grip positions, No-screw leverage mount, 300-pound rated capacity.
strengths: 300-pound rating and 5 grip positions at a genuinely budget price
Most-rated bar in the entire category, a long track record at this price
Doubles as a floor unit for push-ups, dips, and sit-ups
limitations: Only fits doorways up to 32 inches
Foam grips wear noticeably by year two of daily use

products.name: Yes4All Doorway Pull Up Bar (24-34 Inch)
products.blurb: Key specs: Fits doorways 24 to 34 inches, 200-pound rated capacity, No-screw leverage mount.
strengths: The lowest price of any genuine pull-up bar in this category
Wide 24 to 34 inch fit range covers most standard doorways
limitations: 200-pound capacity is the lowest rating in this list
Thinner grip padding than the pricier Iron Gym or ProsourceFit
Fewer practical grip positions given the bar's shorter length

products.name: Yes4All Heavy Duty Doorway Pull Up Bar (300 lb)
products.blurb: Key specs: 300-pound rated capacity, Fits doorways 30 to 38 inches, Reinforced steel bar.
strengths: 300-pound rating is unusual at this price point
Reinforced bar feels sturdier than the base Yes4All model
limitations: Requires a 30-inch minimum doorway, ruling out narrower frames
Fewer grip positions than the pricier Iron Gym Extreme Edition

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
